site.name: Moony
site.tagline: Your whole net worth. Only on your computer.
site.description: Moony is a free, open-source personal finance app for macOS, Windows and Linux. Bank accounts, investments, crypto, property, loans and insurance in one encrypted database on your own computer. No account, no cloud, no telemetry.

footer.blurb: A personal wealth manager that stays on your computer.
footer.disclaimer: Moony is not financial, tax or investment advice. Figures depend on data from third parties and may be inaccurate.
footer.nocookies: This site sets no cookies and loads nothing from third parties.

install.title: Install and first launch
install.unsigned: The installers are not code-signed yet. Signing needs an Apple Developer Program membership and a Windows code-signing certificate, which the project does not have; it is planned. Until then macOS and Windows show a warning the first time you open the app. The app is not damaged: follow the steps below once. Updates inside the app are verified with the project's own signature either way.

mac.terminal: Open **Terminal** (Applications → Utilities) and run this once:
mac.why: It removes the “downloaded from the internet” mark that makes macOS say “Moony is damaged and can't be opened” (Gatekeeper). Then open Moony as usual.
mac.alt: If macOS instead says it cannot verify the developer, you can also go to **System Settings → Privacy & Security** (on macOS 12 and earlier: **System Preferences → Security & Privacy**), scroll to **Security** and click **Open Anyway** next to Moony.

win.keep: Download the installer. If the browser says the file is not commonly downloaded, keep it (in Edge: **⋯ → Keep → Show more → Keep anyway**).
win.run: Run it. Windows SmartScreen may show “Windows protected your PC”. Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**.

linux.fuse: Some distributions need the `libfuse2` package for AppImages.

first.title: First run
first.intro: A brief, skippable welcome animation leads into a setup wizard. It walks you through:
steps: Your **recovery key**. Save it: it is the only way to reset a forgotten password, and it works only together with the key files in the data folder, so back up your data too (**Settings → Data and backups**).
An offer to add your first account and import a bank statement.
first.outro: The dashboard then shows a Getting started checklist.

updating.title: Updating
updating.text: After you unlock Moony, it asks GitHub whether a newer version exists and offers a one-click update. The download is verified against the project's public key before it is installed. You can switch the automatic check off in **Settings**; what it sends is listed on the [Privacy page](privacy).

requirements.title: System requirements
requirements.mac: Apple Silicon and Intel Macs. This release does not declare a minimum macOS version; if Moony does not open on an older one, [tell us in GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/fiiles/Moony/discussions).
requirements.win: Windows 10 and 11, 64-bit. Moony needs the Microsoft Edge WebView2 runtime, which is preinstalled on both; the installer fetches it if it is missing.
requirements.linux: x86_64 only: an AppImage, a `.deb` for Debian and Ubuntu and an `.rpm` for Fedora and openSUSE.

sitePrivacy.description: What the Moony website does and does not do: no cookies, no analytics, nothing loaded from third parties, hosted on Cloudflare.
sitePrivacy.title: Privacy of this website
sitePrivacy.intro: This page is about moonyfinance.com. What the Moony app stores and sends is described on the [Privacy page](privacy).

cookies.title: No cookies, no analytics
cookies.text: This website sets no cookies and has no analytics, counters or tracking pixels.

origin.title: Nothing from third parties
origin.text: Fonts, styles and images come from this site's own origin, and the pages make no requests to third parties. A strict Content-Security-Policy header enforces this in the browser, and anyone can check the response headers and network requests in the browser's developer tools.

hosting.title: Hosting
hosting.text: The site is hosted on Cloudflare. Its edge servers see the usual request data, such as your IP address and user agent, under [Cloudflare's privacy policy](https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/). The project keeps Cloudflare's analytics and every other feature that adds scripts or cookies switched off.

downloads.title: Downloads
downloads.text: The download links lead to releases on GitHub, which serves the files.

operator.title: Operator and contact
operator.text: The operator is Filip Král. Questions go to [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/fiiles/Moony/discussions).

free.a: Yes: Moony is open source under the AGPL-3.0 licence, with no paid tier, no trial and no account.

warning.q: Why does my computer warn me when I open it?
warning.a: The installers are not signed with Apple and Microsoft certificates yet, which is planned; until then macOS and Windows warn once, though the app is not damaged. Updates are signed by the project and verified before they install.

data.q: Does Moony collect any data about me?
data.a: No: the app has no analytics, crash reports or usage statistics. Its only requests are for prices, exchange rates and the update check, listed in full on the Privacy page.

password.q: What if I forget my password?
password.a: Use the 24-character recovery key Moony showed you at setup; it is the only way to reset a password. If you lose both, nobody can open your data, so keep a backup (Settings → Data and backups).

devices.q: Can I use it on two computers, or on my phone?
devices.a: No: Moony is desktop only and does not sync, because sync means a server. You can move your data to another computer with a backup file.

bank.q: Does it connect to my bank?
bank.a: No: you import the CSV statements you export from your bank, with 16 presets and column detection for other files. A bank connection would put a third party between you and your data.
